summary: The National Green Tribunal sought the Centre's response to a plea challenging the environmental clearance for a Rs 17,700 crore data centre in Visakhapatnam. The plea says the project threatens a drinking water reservoir and was cleared without adequate assessment of impact on a nearby wildlife sanctuary.
source_title: Bar & Bench — NGT seeks Centre's response to plea against clearance for Google-Adani's Vizag data centre
verbatim: The National Green Tribunal (NGT) has sought the Central government's response to a plea challenging the environmental clearance granted for a ₹17,700 crore data centre project being developed as part of Google and Adani Group's artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure initiative in Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh. The plea alleges that the project threatens a drinking water reservoir and was granted environmental clearance without adequate assessment of its impact on a nearby wildlife sanctuary.
notes: Case caption per Bar & Bench: Boddu Reddy v. Union of India (litigant named in caption). Appellant identity conflict unresolved: B&B page text names no appellant beyond caption; a secondary report names a former GVMC corporator. The 512 MW Adavivaram/Mudasarlova site, 10 Jun 2026 clearance, 750 m/470 m distances and 26 Oct listing come from secondary search summaries and are NOT in the verbatim; not used in summary. Event date = B&B article date (16 Oct 2026); NGT notice date not stated.

summary: An Instagram reel by independent journalists with Tarluvada residents on the Google data centre was withheld in India from 22 May 2026 under a government blocking order. It was accessible again on 10 September 2026, with no reasons given for the block or its reversal.
source_title: Internet Freedom Foundation — 'Dirty Data' reel on Google's Vizag data centre back online in India after 111-day takedown
verbatim: The reel had been blocked since May 22, 2026 under section 79(3)(b) of the IT Act, 2000 through the opaque Sahyog Portal. The reel is back, but the reasons for its blocking, and for its restoration, remain unknown.
notes: Stance describes the takedown, not the project: the reel's own content is critical of the project, and the record records the suppression. Primary here is IFF (the Wire article is bot-walled; its 'restored after three-month takedown' headline was read via search only, not verbatim). Blocking-order details (issuing police officer, unrelated named third party) deliberately omitted: the order's named third party is a private individual. Journalists not named. Single source (IFF) for the restoration; the Wire corroborates by headline only.

summary: A public interest petition before the Andhra Pradesh High Court challenges the Google-Adani Visakhapatnam data centre's environmental clearance and the allotment of 160 acres of temple land. The report's headline says the State claims steps were taken to protect the environment.
source_title: LiveLaw — PIL in AP High Court challenges Google-Adani data centre project at Visakhapatnam
verbatim: A PIL has been filed before the Andhra Pradesh High Court challenging the proposed Google-Adani data centre in Visakhapatnam, questioning the project's Environmental Clearance and the allotment of 160 acres of land for the project. The proposed project includes 160 acres of temple land belonging to Sri Varaha Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Devasthanam, Simhachalam.
notes: Date = LiveLaw article date (14 Sep 2026); filing/notice dates conflict across secondary reports (1 Jul per LiveLaw-linked summary, 24 Aug per TNM, 9 Sep per Plutus) and are unreconciled, so the event date is the report date. Petitioner (an environmental activist) not named. Constituency 'ngo' chosen for an advocacy PIL with no organisation identified; curator may prefer residents. Interim status-quo request not granted per secondary summary (not verbatim): do not state in summary unless verified. Stance rests on the petition, not a finding. Summary's State-claim sentence rests on the LiveLaw headline only (not in the verbatim).

summary: Green Visakhapatnam, a non-profit, objected to the proposed 500 MW Vizag Hyperscale Data Centre, alleging environmental regulation violations and warning of risks to city water and public health. It says the 160 acres of Simhachalam Devasthanam land were allocated without an environmental impact assessment or public consultation.
source_title: Deccan Chronicle — Green Visakhapatnam flags risks from data centre project
verbatim: Green Visakhapatnam has raised objections to the proposed 500-MW Vizag Hyperscale Data Centre project, alleging violations of environmental regulations and warning of its possible impact on public health and the city's water resources. He alleged that the government had allocated 160 acres of land belonging to the Simhachalam Devasthanam at Adivivaram and Mudasarlova to Google and Adani Data Centre without conducting an environmental impact assessment or seeking public opinion.
notes: Organisation's honorary president deliberately not named (private individual). The report places the project at Arilova; the 160 acres are described as Adivivaram/Mudasarlova. Official denial of fast-tracking and the 'guaranteed' 20-year water promise are in secondary summaries only (not verbatim). Duplicates nothing in seed: the existing in-resp-visakha-livelihood is an NST/Reuters item, a different statement. Same 500 MW figure differs from the 512 MW in the NGT plea and the 1 GW hub figure; reported as stated.

summary: Dalit farmers in Tarluvada, Visakhapatnam district, have refused to give up land for the Google AI hub, citing displacement from land allotted to Dalit families in the 1970s and compensation they call below market value. Reporting says the local Dalit community is divided over the project.
source_title: The Business Standard — Giant data centre over land belonging to Dalits sparking protests in Andhra Pradesh
verbatim: Local farmers, including Dalit women, have refused to give up their land, saying they will not be coerced despite political pressure. Frontline further reported that the local Dalit community is divided over the project, with local leaders split in their views
notes: Article relays The Wire and Frontline; those are not cited directly, so single_source is True. The 1970s allotment and below-market compensation claims are in the article body but not in the verbatim, so they are summarised only from the body (not probe-verified). Compensation figures conflict: TOI-cited Rs 17 lakh/20 lakh per acre and 2.5x multiplier are not used. Pairs with, but does not duplicate, the Guardian/TNW land record already seeded. Stance 'mixed' reflects the reported split, not a single position. Event date = article date (1 Jun 2026); the 28 Apr 2026 foundation-stone ceremony is in the body only.

summary: Activists in Andhra Pradesh are demanding a moratorium on new data centres across the state until independent environmental and social impact evaluations are published. The demand is reported in an AFP-sourced feature on resident fears over water, power and jobs at the Google Visakhapatnam hub.
source_title: Malay Mail (AFP) — 'Why here?' India activists demand moratorium as Google's AI hub scars land and sparks water fears
verbatim: Activists in Andhra Pradesh are also demanding a moratorium on new data centres across the state until independent environmental and social impact evaluations are published.
notes: Activist quoted in the article is a private individual of a local campaign group: not named. Attribution to the Human Rights Forum appears in the body and the HRF is an organisation, but the verbatim carries only the demand, so 'ngo' is set on the campaign itself. Water/power/jobs fears are body text, not in the verbatim. The 'Finnish authority halt' is a separate Google site outside India, not used here.

summary: Residents' group Wake Up Thanekar disputes the Balkum data centre's closed-loop, air-cooled water claim. Activists note Amazon disclosed a water need of 125 kilolitres a day while the municipal corporation has agreed to supply 12 million litres a day of recycled sewage water.
source_title: Free Press Journal — Amazon defends Balkum hyperscale data centre as Thanekars demand its relocation
verbatim: Activists have raised doubts about the data centre being a fully closed-loop air-cooled system, highlighting that while Amazon had disclosed to the state government in August 2025 about the requirement of only 125 kilo litres of water per day, the TMC has agreed to supply a whopping 12 million litres per day of recycled sewage water to the facility.
notes: Water dispute is the activists' reading of the disclosed figures, not an official finding; the 125 kL/day vs 12 ML/day gap is reported, not reconciled (Amazon's own 0.01 MLD statement is body text, not verbatim). Civic group president deliberately not named; the TMC commissioner and the Maharashtra CM are named in the article but not in this record. Distinct from in-resp-thane-balkum-residents (same article date) which covers the protest and review demand. Event date = article date (18 Jul 2026).

summary: A protective wall at the under-construction Google-Adani site in Simhachalam-Mudasarlova collapsed on 22 September 2026 after heavy rain. Residents suspect construction has blocked natural drainage, which the report links to questions about the site's environmental clearances.
source_title: The South First — Data center boundary wall collapses in Simhachalam; doubts raised over environmental clearances
verbatim: On Tuesday, 22 September, night, a boundary wall of the under-construction Google-Adani data center in the Simhachalam-Mudasarlova area of Visakhapatnam collapsed. Residents suspect that ongoing construction work has diverted or blocked several natural drainage streams that previously existed in the area.
notes: Cause is attributed to heavy rain and runoff in the article; the drainage link is resident suspicion, which is why the summary says 'residents suspect'. No official finding of cause in the source. Event is a site incident, so it is filed as a response to keep it on the record. The article also mentions an HRF-condemned restriction of a 'Stop Vizag Data Centers' Instagram account (not read in full; not added).

summary: The Human Rights Forum condemned the restriction in India of the 'Stop Vizag Data Centers' Instagram account, which the campaign says reached 56 lakh views and 11,800 followers in two months. HRF says posts by many organisations and individuals critical of AI data centres have been restricted in India.
source_title: The South First — HRF condemns restriction of 'Stop Vizag Data Centers' Instagram account
verbatim: HRF said numerous posts from organisations and individual accounts critical of AI data centres have been restricted on Instagram in India. The 'Stop Vizag Data Centers' campaign had, in barely two months, attracted 56 lakh views and 11,800 followers
notes: Restriction date (19 Sep 2026 per the campaign, via the countercurrents reprint in search) is not in the verbatim; the record is dated to the statement (22 Sep 2026, verified in the article). Campaign view and follower counts are the campaign's own figures, reported as HRF's statement. The IT Rules / Section 79(3)(b) basis is not verified on the South First page and is omitted. The earlier HRF post restrictions (31 May 2026) are not verified and not added. Meta's position not found.
